q: What is the carbon footprint of packaged drinking water per litre?
title: Packaged water carbon footprint per litre
short: For bottled water the bottle usually matters most. Add PET preforms, caps, labels and shrink wrap by weight, then RO, ozonation and filling electricity, and delivery. Divide by litres filled. A 20 litre returnable jar reused many times carries far less packaging per litre.

ul: PET preform per bottle: weigh it; lighter preforms cut the largest line.
HDPE caps, labels and LDPE shrink film.
20 litre polycarbonate or PET jars: divide their footprint by the number of trips each jar makes before it is retired.
Borewell pumps, RO membranes, UV and ozonation.
Blow moulding if you blow your own bottles.

p: Water is heavy, so delivery emissions per litre are noticeable. Count truck diesel for your own fleet as Scope 1, and hired transport as Scope 3.

example.title: Worked example: water plant per litre (one month)
lines: Generator and delivery diesel: 2,500 litres x 2.68 = 6,700 kg CO2
Plant total: 42,200 / 2,000,000 = 0.021 kg CO2 per litre
Add PET, caps, labels and film for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
